lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals and Building a Fueling Meal
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: nonjudgmental noticing

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice nonjudgmental noticing. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Across one ordinary day, the learner pauses four separate times to notice what their body is signaling right then, names the signal in a private notebook using neutral words, and picks one helpful response to try for that signal without rating themselves as good or bad for having it.
safetyNotes: Notebook entries are private; a guardian may see the completion status but not the raw entries themselves.
No weight, size, calorie, or body-shape language is used anywhere in this task, by the learner or in feedback.
materials: learner-local: a pencil or typing device

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Which signal was hardest to notice or name today, and what made noticing it harder than the others?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Neutral language: All four entries use only the five neutral signal words with no judgment or body-size language. | Signal-to-clue accuracy: Each clue plausibly matches its named signal. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner notice the same signal at two different times of day and compare, in writing, whether the clue or the helpful response changed between the two moments.

duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: nonjudgmental noticing worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Across one ordinary day, the learner pauses four separate times to notice what their body is signaling right then, names the signal in a private notebook using neutral words, and picks one helpful response to try for that signal without rating themselves as good or bad for having it.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact nonjudgmental noticing decision or action.
Model move 2: Before the day starts, review the five signal words with your adult: hunger, thirst, tiredness, boredom, stress.
Model move 3: With your adult, practice one full round: notice a signal right now, name it using a neutral word, and say one response you could try.
Model check: Neutral language: All four entries use only the five neutral signal words with no judgment or body-size language. | Signal-to-clue accuracy: Each clue plausibly matches its named signal.

resources.title: nonjudgmental noticing action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for nonjudgmental noticing.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: nonjudgmental noticing coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Across one ordinary day, the learner pauses four separate times to notice what their body is signaling right then, names the signal in a private notebook using neutral words, and picks one helpful response to try for that signal without rating themselves as good or bad for having it.
Coach direction: Before the day starts, review the five signal words with your adult: hunger, thirst, tiredness, boredom, stress.
Learner prompt: For each of the five signal words, write one plain-language clue your own body gives you when that signal shows up (for example, a clue for tiredness, not a definition of the word).
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: nonjudgmental noticing complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult, practice one full round: notice a signal right now, name it using a neutral word, and say one response you could try.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I named the signal using one of the five neutral words, not a judgment word.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I named the clue in my body that told me the signal was there.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I named one response I could try, without deciding whether the signal itself was good or bad.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: nonjudgmental noticing minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which signal was hardest to notice or name today, and what made noticing it harder than the others?

Success checks: Neutral language: All four entries use only the five neutral signal words with no judgment or body-size language. | Signal-to-clue accuracy: Each clue plausibly matches its named signal.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: nonjudgmental noticing supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional nonjudgmental noticing condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Neutral language: All four entries use only the five neutral signal words with no judgment or body-size language. | Signal-to-clue accuracy: Each clue plausibly matches its named signal..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u04-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
